text:
Jordan: Heads-up — noticed a mismatch in the deploy authz matrix vs actual rolebindings for the nodepool provisioner. Some deploys are succeeding but audit shows KMS decrypts coming from a different svcacct than the RBAC entries.
Alyssa: :eyes: repro steps?
Jordan: I saw it on 2999501200 while chasing a failed gpu job. Quick snippet from audit: `auth: {"user":"system:serviceaccount:infra:nodepool-provisioner","impersonated_user":"system:serviceaccount:deploy:deployer"} action=decrypt status=200` — but RoleBinding only grants `deploy:deployer` decrypt to kms-wrap role in `deploy` ns.
Sam: hmm, so the request is impersonated? Could be our deploy proxy doing SA impersonation, and the nodepool-provisioner has broader cluster role that allows impersonate.
Mike: I pulled the rolebindings:```kubectl get rolebinding -n deploy nodepool-deploy-binding -o yaml
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deployer
  namespace: deploy
roleRef:
  name: kms-wrap
```But the nodepool-provisioner has a ClusterRoleBinding `nodepool-provisioner-crb` with subject `system:serviceaccount:infra:nodepool-provisioner` and it includes `impersonate` on svcacct tokens in AKS.```
Tess: If impersonation is allowed, then the effective principal doing KMS decrypts could be the impersonated SA, which would explain audit line. Do we have KMS policy limiting by principal identity or by SA name?
Jordan: KMS policy is layered: we target the service account name in the KMS envelope access log, so mismatch matters.
Alyssa: This seems like an authz matrix mismatch: our declarative matrix says only `deploy:deployer` should have kms unwrap, but cluster-level impersonation lets infra SA escalate.
Sam: Proposed short-term: add an explicit Deny via a namespace-scoped PSP/OPA constraint? Or patch the nodepool-provisioner ClusterRole to remove `impersonate` on `serviceaccounts` and instead grant a narrower set.
Mike: For quick mitigation I can add a temporary rolebinding that revokes `impersonate` by overwriting the CRB, but that's disruptive. Alternative: add an auditbackfill job that enumerates recent decrypts and maps impersonator -> impersonated, to scope blast radius.
Tess: I can run the backfill: query stackdriver logs for protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail contains `nodepool-provisioner` and filter KMS decrypt API calls. Then produce list.
Jordan: Cool — please include last 7 days and link to ticket. Add the auditbackfill results to the incident ticket (infra-4234).
deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4234 and linked this thread: https://redwood.internal/t/INFRA-4234
Alyssa: After backfill, let's schedule a quick config change to remove impersonation from nodepool CRB, then run a canary deploy to ensure no regression.
Sam: Also worth adding a unit test to our deploy-proxy that forbids cross-namespace impersonation unless explicitly allowlisted.
Mike: I'll draft the CR change and a rollback plan. If we touch CRBs we should coordinate with oncall window tomorrow 0100-0300 UTC.
Tess: Backfill job finished (summary): 42 decrypt events in 7d where `nodepool-provisioner` was the authn principal and 17 of those had an impersonated SA from `deploy` ns. Pushing csv to INFRA-4234.
Jordan: That's actionable. Let's do: (1) emergency CRB prune to remove `impersonate` for serviceaccounts, (2) deploy-proxy test/guard, (3) KMS policy review to include both principal and source IP where possible.
Alyssa: Agree. Can we also add an alert rule for anomalous impersonation counts > 5/hr?
Sam: I'll open a follow-up RFC to modify authz matrix and add tests.
Mike: Will prepare CR and run it in staging first.
Jordan: Thanks everyone. Will own incident runbook update and postmortem template after this stabilizes. Keep updates in INFRA-4234 thread. :white_check_mark:
